Stated Claim / Post Context:
Blacklock, Birmingham B3: ‘A very, very cool version of an Angus Steakhouse’ – restaurant review

The chophouse chain has taken its big flavours to the UK’s second city

Actual Article Body:
Ever-open, eminently relatable, sensibly priced spots of this sort will always have an audience

A London chophouse has taken up residence on St Philip’s Place, Birmingham, on the edge of Cathedral Square, or “Pigeon Park”, as the locals call it. This particular nook of Brum city centre is a magnet to those feathered blighters, although Blacklock’s smoulderingly macho menu is ironically pigeon-meat free, revolving instead around heaps of chops and steaks cooked over charcoal. There’s porterhouse, bone-in sirloin, lamb rump and pig’s head on toast.

Launched in London in 2015, Blacklock was the elegant, edgy, no-nonsense dining experience for groovy young things who quite literally wanted meat and two veg, so long as said veg was dripping-fat chips; it now has five sites in the capital and another in Manchester. “We just ended up at Blacklock,” people used to tell me half a dozen times a week, then go on to rave about the bread, the gravy and the ash-baked sweet potatoes, and revel in the glorious simplicity of it all. Modern life was complex, Blacklock was not, but neither was it cheap enough to feel like a jaunt down the Toby Carvery. And now its big flavours and broad appeal have hit the UK’s second city.

It has rather brilliantly taken over the ground floor of St Philip’s House, a former Victorian vicarage. There’s masses of dark wood panelling stripped back to the original and, reportedly, a disused tunnel below, destination unclear. Another evil dimension, perhaps? Safe to say, Blacklock is a gothic gourmand’s paradise. It’s pretty hard to get a table round here, because it’s a magnet for tourists and Tinder dates, and the Ivy and Damascena on Temple Row and the nearby Pasture are always, always jam-packed. It’s a Monday night, and we feel lucky to get a walk-in, though Blacklock stresses that it officially welcomes them, and will happily put you up in the bar until your wishes can be granted.
 
 
 Blacklock Birmingham already feels much more fun than Blacklock London, because, let’s be honest, things are a lot less aloof north of Watford. Our server, a naughty, rollicking bundle of joy, tempts us with potted meat with kimchi, egg-and-anchovy bites and glasses of Westwell Pelegrim, an English sparkling from Kent. These bites are perfectly functional little affairs, if a bit dry, and leave me wishing I’d ordered the crayfish cocktail or the mushrooms on toast.

Next, a stainless-steel tureen heaped with lamb cutlets and lamb T-bones at £8 a chop...
